concept: Nautical-dawn fog-harvester repair across mist, mesh occluders, droplets, cliffs, and ocean depth
negative_en: fake-looking background, 3D render look, low resolution, excessive HDR, unrealistic hands, cartoon style, body distortion, over-processed retouching, plastic-looking skin, distorted fingers
prompt_en: A photorealistic environmental documentary photograph at a working coastal fog-harvesting station at nautical dawn. One visibly adult field technician stands in a roofless service bay between towering dew-beaded mesh collectors. Their visible adult face, hair, complexion, and general appearance are visually continuous with the supplied appearance reference; the reference supplies long dark wavy hair with a visible part and the overall adult face and skin rendering. The technician tightens a torn mesh panel with a hand tensioning tool while guiding fresh condensate into a graduated glass cylinder. Use a medium-wide eye-level 35 mm three-quarter view: the face, hands, tool, tube, and cylinder remain readable, close-focus droplets and a coiled translucent hose occupy the foreground, and staggered mesh rows, a narrow service track, pale cliffs, and ocean recede behind. From the low ocean horizon, one coherent source direction anchors every visible shaft; a window cloud foliage architecture or gobo provides identifiable occlusion gaps, realized here by the staggered fog-harvesting mesh. Sea mist fulfills how haze dust mist or atmosphere makes the light path visible within volume. Across the wet scene, separate bright shafts and darker gaps preserve the occluder's pattern, and at least one shaft lands plausibly on a subject floor wall or atmospheric layer, visibly crossing the technician, service floor, and nearest mesh. Cool blue mist and restrained amber dawn light reveal damp metal, natural fabric, believable water, and weathered fasteners.
